# Resource: Golden Reject Set (2026-07-16)

**Status**: Operator ground truth. On 2026-07-15 the operator reviewed the
first real generated batch (`outreach-engine/out/first-100-2026-07-14.csv`,
5 packages) in the review dashboard and **rejected 5/5**. These messages are
kept verbatim as regression fixtures: any strengthened quality gate
(Amendment 1, spec.md FR-029–FR-034) MUST fail every message below. A gate
that passes any of them is not strict enough.

**Source**: `outreach-engine/out/first-100-2026-07-14.csv`, generated by
`scripts/first-100.ts` (which bypassed the Anti-Values Linter entirely —
see Amendment 1 context).

## Defect classes observed

| # | Class | Which packages |
|---|-------|----------------|
| D1 | False deliverable claim: "I made you a short personal video" appended deterministically; no video existed, `{{BFV_LINK}}` unresolved | all 5 |
| D2 | Speculative, unevidenced pain ("Your team must spend hours…", "I bet your team gets asked…") | Mozilla, Basecamp, Example Domain |
| D3 | Self-contradiction / double ask: body asks "Can I show you how in a quick video?" then CTA asserts the video already exists | Mozilla, Basecamp, Sivers |
| D4 | Non-viable prospect confidently packaged (example.com is not a business; pain point invented) | Example Domain |
| D5 | Creepy/arbitrary fact use ("You met 17 people in Jakarta and 16 in Kuala Lumpur") — extraction surfaced blog trivia, model weaponized it | Sivers |
| D6 | `needs_research` row still produced a send-shaped message + video claim | No Website Co |
| D7 | Forced 3rd-grade simplicity + speculation reads as baby-talk spam, not an adult who did homework | all 5 |

## Rejected messages (verbatim)

### 1. Mozilla (Mitchell) — D1, D2, D3, D7

> Hi Mitchell, I use Firefox every day, so thank you for that. Here is my
> thought. Mozilla helps people in many languages all over the world. That
> means a lot of questions and bug reports come in each day. Your team must
> spend hours sorting them by hand. AI can read each one, sort it, and
> answer the easy ones fast. That frees your people for the hard work. Can
> I show you how in a short clip?
>
> I made you a short personal video. Watch it here: {{BFV_LINK}}

### 2. Basecamp (Jason) — D1, D2, D3, D7

> Hi Jason, I saw you pride yourself on great customer service. That is
> rare these days! But I bet your team gets asked the same things a lot,
> like 'Can I link up Google Docs?' or 'Can I hide unfinished work?' That
> eats up time. I can set up AI to answer those fast, so your team can
> focus on the hard stuff. Can I show you how in a quick video?
>
> I made you a short personal video. Watch it here: {{BFV_LINK}}

### 3. Derek Sivers — D1, D3, D5, D7

> Hi Derek. You met 17 people in Jakarta and 16 in Kuala Lumpur. That is a
> lot of emails to read and sort by hand. I bet it eats up your day. I
> built a tool that reads your emails and lines up your meetups for you, so
> you keep the real talks and skip the busy work. Want to see a quick video
> of how it works?
>
> I made you a short personal video. Watch it here: {{BFV_LINK}}

### 4. Example Domain (Alex) — D1, D2, D4, D7

> Hi Alex, I saw your site lets people use a domain for docs examples
> without asking first. That is smart. But it can be hard to help every
> user who has a question about using it the right way. What if a smart
> bot could answer those questions fast, all day? Would you be open to a

>
> I made you a short personal video. Watch it here: {{BFV_LINK}}

### 5. No Website Co (Jordan) — D1, D6

> Hi Jordan, I looked into No Website Co and had an idea to save you time.
> Worth a quick look?
>
> I made you a short personal video. Watch it here: {{BFV_LINK}}
